text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike for tenant=helio-pay on prod-us-west · p95=420ms (baseline ~120ms), p99=3.9s (baseline ~1.1s). Streaming stalls and increased error rate. Paging oncall.

ryan (oncall): on it. I see paging from latency-monitor. Any immediate customer impact?

support-helio: HelioPay reports slow completions and streaming disconnects for some users, happening around 21:14 UTC. They called out long receipts + embedded base64 blobs in prompts.

maria (ml-infra): quick glance at metrics: sustained increase in kv_cache_evictions for tenant helio-pay since 20:58 UTC, evictions/sec jumped x30. Also a spike in concurrent streaming connections for that tenant. suspect K/V cache thrash + high concurrency.

liz (eng-sre): can you dump a small snippet of logs for a few requests? look for "streaming stall" or "kv_cache_miss" entries.

ryan (oncall): grabbing logs from router and runtime for helio-pay. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T20:59:02Z] tenant=helio-pay request_id=abc123 stage=runtime kv_cache_miss=true kv_cache_eviction=true seq_len=2048 model=gpt-j-quant
[2026-03-15T20:59:02Z] tenant=helio-pay request_id=abc123 stage=streaming stall=true stall_ms=1200
[2026-03-15T21:00:10Z] tenant=helio-pay request_id=def456 kv_cache_eviction_count=27 active_streams=412
```
Notable: seq_len frequently > 1500 and we have repeated cache evictions per request.

maria (ml-infra): that matches the KV cache thrash hypothesis — long prefixes (repeated unique prefixes caused by attachments) push out useful cache entries. With high concurrency this degrades per-token perf and triggers stalls.

ashley (product-ops): HelioPay is a single-tenant customer on Dedicated pool helio-prod-*. They are on our reserved capacity cluster; we should avoid full cluster restarts if possible. Customer is sensitive — please keep them updated.

liz (eng-sre): mitigation plan (short-lived):
- throttle tenant concurrency to 25 (was 200)
- temporarily disable streaming for helio-pay to avoid stall/reconnect loops
- clear tenant KV cache slices for helio-pay
- if needed, route helio-pay to lower-capacity but stable model (gpt-neoq-7b-fb) as fallback
I'll run these in order and report.

ryan (oncall): applying throttle now: `redwoodctl tenancy update helio-pay --max-concurrency 25` -> OK.

ops-bot: deploy job accepted: tenancy/update/2187654321-1 -> queued on infra-worker-4.

ryan (oncall): disabled streaming flag for tenant: `redwoodctl tenancy set-flag helio-pay disable_streaming=true` -> OK. Notifying support to tell customer: disabling streaming will fall back to non-streaming completions.

support-helio: noted. Please confirm expected UX impact so we can tell HelioPay.

ryan (oncall): temporary UX impact: responses may appear after generation completes instead of streaming, but should be more stable.

liz (eng-sre): clearing KV cache shards for helio-pay: `runtime-admin clear-kvcache --tenant helio-pay --shard 3` -> executed across 3 shards.

maria (ml-infra): while throttle and cache clear rolling, I'm preparing a model-route fallback: route helio-pay to gpt-neoq-7b-fb (quantized) for 10% of traffic, 100% if we see continued degradation. low risk and faster to spin up on dedicated pool.

ryan (oncall): observed metrics 2m after throttle/cache clear: p99 dropped from 3.9s -> 1.6s, p95 ~180ms. active_streams down to ~60. error rate decreased.

ashley (product-ops): please post the customer-facing status update (short) for HelioPay: we’re mitigating and will follow up.

support-helio: sending update to HelioPay: "We've throttled concurrency and temporarily disabled streaming to stabilize responses. We're continuing to investigate root cause and will update within 60 minutes."

maria (ml-infra): rolling the 10% fallback route now: `routes apply helio-pay --model gpt-neoq-7b-fb --weight 10` -> OK. observing no error delta for fallback requests.

liz (eng-sre): summary of immediate outcome: KV cache thrash caused by highly variable long prefixes + high concurrency -> evictions -> increased compute per request -> streaming stalls. Short-term mitigations (throttle, disable streaming, clear cache, fallback model) reduced p99 to ~1.2s and stabilized errors.

ryan (oncall): restarting one misbehaving runtime pod helio-prod-3 (soft restart) because it had high CPU and repeated stall logs. `kubectl rollout restart pod/helio-prod-3` -> pod restarted and rejoined. no crash loops.

ops-bot: restart job completed: helio-prod-3 ready in 38s.

ashley (product-ops): thanks team. Requesting a short RCA and follow-up plan for HelioPay (postmortem + config changes) before EOD. They may want guardrails to avoid long-prefix attacks.

liz (eng-sre): next steps assigned:
- maria to propose KV cache sizing + eviction policy change for single-tenant Dedicated pools (action: adjust shard allocation)
- ryan to produce timeline and commands executed (this thread covers it)
- product to work with HelioPay on input validation / prompt size limits (ashley)
- schedule follow-up meeting with HelioPay for 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC
I'll own the on-call follow-up until 02:00 UTC, then hand off to night oncall.

ryan (oncall): dropping a short timeline and metrics into support ticket now. p99 graph attached to ticket.

support-helio: HelioPay acknowledged the temporary fix and asked for more details about long prefixes. they want an ETA for full fix.

liz (eng-sre): for the postmortem we'll include: root cause hypothesis (prompt-length-driven KV thrash), why autoscaling/eviction didn't prevent impact, and permanent mitigations (tenant-level concurrency caps, prompt-length soft limits, per-tenant cache sizing, better fallback routing).

maria (ml-infra): also recommend adding a tenant-level circuit breaker that auto-disables streaming when repeated stall patterns are detected for that tenant.

ryan (oncall): logging handoff: I'll update the incident channel if anything regresses. handing follow-up to liz (eng-sre) at 02:00 UTC.

liz (eng-sre): taking over for post-incident work. Will open a formal incident doc and link here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
